description: Portrait-art rows for story-script characters: one clothing texture name and a list of facial-expression texture names per character costume.

ID.simple: Costume row id used by ScriptCharacter rows.
ID.technical: FName row key (export ImportKeyField Id). GameStoryDemoImage_FindClothesRow resolves it inside ScriptCharacterClothesDataTables after selecting ScriptCharacter.Id_ScriptCharacterClothes[ClothesIndex]; exported ids are <character>_<costume> (e.g. CP_010_00).

ClothesFileName.simple: Dynamic-load texture name for the costume overlay.
ClothesFileName.technical: FName passed to FindDynamicLoadTexture and installed as the material's Character_Clothes texture parameter; NAME_None clears it (nullptr). Exported values follow T_UI_STDM_<id>.

FacialFileName.simple: Facial-expression texture names for the costume.
FacialFileName.technical: TArray<FName>; indexed by the uint8 Facial value evaluated by the story-demo character-parameter sequencer track, with an upper-bound check only (Facial >= Num gives NAME_None/nullptr). The selected texture is installed as Character_Facial. Exported rows have 12 slots, including None placeholders; the C++ treats the array as dynamic.

notes: The row struct constructor is empty: no C++ fallback textures or array prefill (Source/AbramsDataTable/Private/GameDataTableRow_ScriptCharacterClothes.cpp:3).

Single table in the exported asset set; no numbered shards or localization variants were found. Row counts and texture-name examples above are observations from the exported asset, not documentation-site guesses.

Evidence comes from the reconstructed C++ in Source/; status/ records byte matches for the GameStoryDemoImage owner TU, but this JSON does not claim a retail byte comparison for every individual helper.

usages.detail: GameStoryDemoImage_FindClothesRow joins ScriptCharacter -> ScriptCharacterClothes; returns null on a bad clothes index or missing row.
UGameStoryDemoImage::SetCharacter loads ClothesFileName/FacialFileName and binds them to the dynamic material.
Sequencer track supplies CharacterId, ClothesIndex and the Facial array index on each evaluation.
Tick loads the single ScriptCharacterClothesDataTable into the manager's ScriptCharacterClothesDataTables array.
